programme.title: Boban is Fuigheag
programme.desc: Tha Fuigheag a’ cluich le rudeigin beag spòrsail a lorg e. Feumaidh Boban obrachadh a-mach cò às a thàinig an rud agus an uairsin a thilleadh air ais. Fuigheag is playing with something he’s found. Boban must work out where the item has come from and return it.

programme.title: Lon le Linda
programme.desc: Tha Linda NicLeòid agus a caraidean a’ dèanamh bonnaich-èisg bhlasta. Linda and her friends make tasty fishcakes.

programme.title: Cleasan Ataidh & Tilidh/The Adventures of Abney & Teal
programme.desc: Tha Nìp a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Tha Tilidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean. Mu dheireadh thall, tha Àtaidh a’ lorg chuibhlichean dha fhèin. Chan eil iad cho cumhachdach an toiseach, ach chan fhada gus am fàs iad ro chumhachdach fiù ’s! Neep and Teal find some wheels. Finally, Abney gets hold of some wheels of his own. They aren't brilliant at first, but soon they become perhaps even a bit too brilliant!

programme.title: Ladybird & Bee/Daolag-bhreac is Seillean
programme.desc: An-diugh, tha Daolag-bhreac is Seillean a’ coinneachadh ri losgann is cinn-pholla bheaga. Today, Ladybird and Bee meet a frog and some small tadpoles.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Nuair a chluinneas Comhachag Sionnach a’ bruidhinn mu Mhaigheach mar a’ charaid as fheàrr a th’ aige, tha Comhachag ag iarraidh a’ cheart rud air a shon fhèin. Aon mhadainn, tha balùn dearg a’ nochdadh ri taobh na craoibhe aige. Seo a’ charaid as fheàrr aig Comhachag! Tha iad a’ dèanamh a h-uile rud còmhla gus an tòiseach am balùn ri searg. Tha Comhachag troimhe chèile. Ciamar idir a thogas Sionnach agus Maigheach a shunnd? When Fox mentions that Hare is his best friend, Owl decides that he needs a best friend, too. One morning, a red balloon suddenly appears near his tree. This is Owl’s new best friend! They do everything together, but then the balloon slowly starts to deflate. Owl is in despair. What can Fox and Hare do to cheer Owl up again?

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachdan do chlann òga. Tha Pàdruig Moireasdan a’ leughadh An Latha Spòrs. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh agus a dhealbhachadh le Nick Butterworth agus Mick Inkpen. Chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Jo NicDhòmhnaill. A bedtime story for young children. Pàdruig Morrison reads An Latha Spòrs, written and illustrated by Nick Butterworth and Mick Inkpen, and translated into Gaelic by Jo Macdonald.

programme.title: Stri
programme.desc: Tha preasantairean CBBC ALBA uabhasach fhèin measail air dùbhlain ach saoil cò shoirbhicheas is Rachel a’ tadhal orra? The CBBC ALBA presenters love a good challenge but who will emerge victorious as Rachel joins them?

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl agus a charaidean a’ dol air turas-sgoile suas an canàl is tha iad a’ dùsgadh seann uilebheist air a bheil An Liobach Mòr. Tha An Liobach Mòr gam putadh thairis air eas, is tha seo gan tilgeil air ais ann an ùine gu àm Diùrasach. Dave and his friends embark on a school trip along the canal, where they awaken an ancient monster called Big Lippy. The beast pushes them over a waterfall and sends them back in time, to the Jurassic era.

programme.title: An Saoghal Droil aig Pol Ploc/The Rubbish World of Dave Spud
programme.desc: Tha Pòl a’ lorg seann chonsail geama coimpiutair aig an dump. Sa gheama feumar sombaidhean a spreadhadh, is tha a charaid, Ceitidh Sombaidh, ga ghabhail san t-sròin. Tha Ceitidh a’ dol às a dhèidh le buidheann de shombaidhean mòr fìor is fiadhaich. Dave finds a handheld computer game at the dump. The game involves killing zombies which his friend, Zombie Katie, finds rather insulting. Exacting her revenge, Dave finds himself confronted with a group of very angry and very real zombies.

programme.title: Na Speuran
programme.desc: Thèid air turas suas dha na speuran cuide ris an Speuradair Zach! Air an turas fànais iongantach seo tha e ag innse dhuinn mu Theileasgop Sheumais Webb. Bidh e cuideachd a’ beachdachadh air a’ cheist mhòr “a bheil sìon beò air planaidean eile?” Blast off into space with Astronaut Zach! In this amazing space voyage, he tells us about the James Webb Telescope and also debates the age-old question: 'Is there life on other planets?'

programme.title: Hilda
programme.desc: Anns an leabhar-lann, tha an leabhraiche feumach air taic bho Hilda is Flòraidh nuair a tha iad a' tighinn tarsainn air Tùr nam Bana-bhuidseach, is nuair a tha aca ri rèiseadh an aghaidh tìm airson leabhar a tha a dhìth a lorg. The librarian needs Hilda and Flòraidh’s help as they come across the Witches Tower, and when they have to race against time to find a missing book.

programme.title: Gàrraidhean Mòra
programme.desc: Mairi travels to Logan Botanic Garden, Scotland’s most exotic garden! Curator Richard Baines shows Mairi some of the many plants that can be grown outdoors at Logan that would need to be kept indoors anywhere else in Scotland. They make their way through the giant Gunnera Bog, before enjoying some mocktails made with plants selected from the garden. Tèarlach Quinnell talks about the various ways that plant protect themselves. Sa phrògram seo, thig Màiri a Ghàrradh Lusan Lògan faisg air an t-Sròn Reamhar – an gàrradh as deòranta an Alba! Seallaidh an Fhear-tasgaidh, Richard Baines, dhith feadhainn dha na lusan a tha fàs a-muigh ann an Lògan a dh’fheumadh an cumail a-staigh an àite sam bith eile an Alba. Thèid iad tro bhog mòr Gunnera mus stad iad airson mocktails air an dèanamh à lusan sa ghàrradh. Innsidh Tèarlach Quinnell dhuinn mu na diofar dhòighean a th’aig lusan iad fhèin a dhìon. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Calum Maclean is on the hunt for a world-famous dish which was created in an Indian restaurant in Glasgow.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Mas Fhior
programme.desc: Niall Iain Macdonald hosts the quiz show where more than general knowledge is required to win. Standing in the way of our two teams from winning are the ‘Pretenders’, who, from the comfort of their own homes, are on a mission to fox our contestants. Which of this week’s teams, Seumas & Innes or Liz Anne & Eilidh, will get the upper hand and have a chance to take home the grand prize? Niall Iain Dòmhnallach le farpais cheist ùr far a bheil barrachd air eòlas coitcheann a dhìth gus buannachadh. Tha na Mas Fhìoraich a’ gabhail pàirt bhon dachaighean ’s ag amas air a’ chùis a dhèanamh air an dà sgioba. Cò aca bho sgiobaidhean na seachdain-sa, Seumas & Innes no Liz Anne & Eilidh, a gheibh làmh an uachdar agus cothrom fhaighinn air an duais mhòr?

programme.title: Chernobyl – Utopia na Smàl/Chernobyl – Utopia in Flames
programme.desc: Tha a’ chiad readhachtar niùclasach foillsichte san t-saoghal na chunnart dhan t-siostam Sobhieteach air fad. Ach, fiù ’s an dèidh dhaibh sgòth rèidio-beò a lorg os cionn an t-Suain, tha Mosgo a’ fuireach sàmhach. Tha e a’ toirt 36 uairean a thìde an dèidh na mòr-thubaist an riaghaltas innse do dhaoine gum feum iad baile Pripyat, a tha a-nis air a thruailleadh, fhàgail. The world's first exposed nuclear reactor is a danger to the entire Soviet system. However, even after the discovery of a radioactive cloud over Sweden, Moscow continues to remain silent. Then, 36 hours after the catastrophe, the Soviet government finally decides to evacuate the contaminated city of Pripyat. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Somhairle Spins
programme.desc: Tha slighe dùbhlanach aig Somhairle agus a bhràthair Innes air a’ chiad latha aca a’ rothaireachd eadar Inbhir Nis agus Glaschu air an Badger Divide. Somhairle and his brother Innes have a challenging start on their first day cycling between Inverness and Glasgow on the Badger Divide.

programme.title: Alba fon Talamh/Scotland Underground
programme.desc: Calum starts his underground tour in the north west of Scotland. With help from local experts, he explores the incredible cave networks of Applecross. Looking at how man has harnessed underground resources, Calum explores the Nevis Tunnels, the aluminium smelter in Fort William and the globally unique Lochaline sand mine. Tha Calum a’ tòiseachadh air a thuras fon talamh ann an Iar-thuath na h-Alba. Le cuideachadh bho eòlaichean-uamha ionadail, rannsachaidh e lìonraidhean uamhan iongantach na Comraich. Chithear mar a tha mac an duine air feum a dhèanamh de ghoireasan fon talamh fhad ’s a nì Calum rannsachadh air Tunailean Nibheis agus leaghadair aluiminium a’ Ghearasdain, cho math ri mèinne gainmhich ann an Loch Àlainn a tha gun shamhail san t-saoghal. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Fraochy Bay
programme.desc: Fàilte gu Fraochy Bay , baile nach fhaic thu a h-uile là! Is iomadh annas a tha ri fhaicinn sa bhaile , agus sin gun ghuth air cail ach muinntir a bhaile fhèin. Tha cobhair a dhith air dannsairean a bhaile agus 's e Murdo Handel gaisgeach na h uaireach. Welcome to the colourful and unusual world of Fraochy Bay, a miniature metropolis somewhere off the fringes of the map. The local dance troupe are in distress, a situation which calls for careful handling of a musical score.

programme.title: Samhradh air Sàl
programme.desc: Angus Mackay is joined by his daughter Ruth as they go to sea on a spectacular summer's day. Along the way they encounter a large pod of dolphins who take great delight in racing their small boat. Then it’s time for fishing and chat about the formative role of fishing in Ruth’s upbringing. Anns an dàrna prògram mu dheireadh san t-sreath, tha nighean Aonghais, Rut, còmhla ris agus iad aig muir air latha samhraidh eireachdail. Air an t-slighe, coinnichidh iad ri buidheann leumadairean-mara a tha dannsa mun eathar. Às dèidh sin, tha an t-àm ann airson iasgach agus còmhradh mun bhuaidh a bh’ aig iasgach air beatha Ruth.

programme.title: Machair
programme.desc: Drama Gàidhlig stèidhichte ann an Leòdhas. Gaelic soap based on the Isle of Lewis.

programme.title: Alleluia!
programme.desc: Prògram spioradail le laoidhean, sailm agus leughaidhean à Coats ann am Pàislig, air a lìbhrigeadh le Iain MacFhionghain. Am measg na seinneadairean bidh Costello MacÌomhair, Maeve NicFhionghain agus Seumas Greumach. Cuideachd, an còisir Soisgeul fo stiùir Gareth Fuller. Bidh Iain fhèin a’ meòrachadh air cuspair creideimh le leughadh agus smuain, dàn is seallaidhean spioradail à Tiriodh ann an companachd Dòmhnall Eachann Meek agus bidh Chloe Steele a’ toirt dhuinn seirm adhraidh air a’ phìob à Manachainn nan Lios. Iain MacKinnon presents a mix of hymns, psalms and readings from Coats in Paisley. Amongst the singers performing are Costello Maciver, Maeve MacKinnon and James Graham. Also appearing is the choir Soisgeul conducted by Gareth Fuller. Iain reflects on his own beliefs with a selected reading and thought, spiritual poetry and landscapes from Tiree in the company of Donald E Meek, and Chloe Steele performs a tune of worship on the pipes from Beauly Priory. In Gaelic with English subtitles

programme.title: Da Vinci: The Lost Treasure
programme.desc: Leonardo da Vinci is considered by many to be one of the greatest artists who ever lived. Yet his reputation rests on only a handful of pictures - including the world's most famous painting, the Mona Lisa. As the National Gallery in London prepares to open its doors on a remarkable exhibition of Leonardo's work, Fiona Bruce travels to Florence, Milan, Paris and Warsaw to uncover the story of this enigmatic genius - and to New York, where she is given an exclusive preview of a sensational discovery: a new Leonardo.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Water has been a flashpoint in the Middle East and worldwide demand is outstripping supply, so how do we make sure there's enough to go round? This most basic resource is vital for drinking, sanitation and agriculture, but also for jobs and economies everywhere. The World Bank's global director for water Saroj Kumar Jha explains why they're trying to make it more of a priority for government spending. And Mareen Schneider, the founder and CEO of project developer Grasshopper Investments, explains how she's coming up with radical new ways for the private sector to invest in water. Plus, Ben Thompson also hears from José Manuel Entrecanales, the CEO of Spanish infrastructure giant Acciona, about the projects they're building around the world and why we need to rethink the value we give to water.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: In this episode, the team try to prevent a barber in Doncaster, who is actually working whilst on the phone, paying out to a tricksy scammer. As the scammer tries to persuade her that he is there to help recover some lost cryptocurrency, the ground team are on the road to her shop to put a stop to the scam. The team have their work cut out to persuade the barber and her colleagues that they are legit – and this particular race against time goes right to the wire.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: In true Escape to the Country style, today’s couple (both former international rugby players) want to leave London in search of a rural idyll in Dorset, and Alistair Appleton is the man to help them on their way. Aside from property, Alistair learns about the health benefits of watercress at a farm which specialises in growing this delicious and nutritious crop.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, flatmates Rachel, Scott, Tara and Daniel – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, flatmates Rachel, Scott, Tara and Daniel – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: Acting on a tip off, the Peelers storm a city centre flat on a drugs bust. Inside, a startled suspect is immediately cuffed and arrested while outside, the PSNI team search the nearby streets for the suspected big-time dealer they think may have fled the scene with more drugs. On Great Victoria Street in Belfast city centre, police attempt to arrest a man who refuses to comply with a search. The situation quickly escalates and he is detained by a number of officers who use a spit guard and leg restraints. The man is taken into custody where he continues to kick off. Officers and custody staff surround the man in his cell as they try to get him under control. Later, Stephen interviews the Deputy Chief Constable, Bobby Singleton, and questions him about some PSNI tactics and officers’ use of force.

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies

programme.title: Limbs in the Loch: Catching a Killer
programme.desc: William Beggs is wanted in connection to the murder of Barry Wallace but has fled the country and handed himself in to police in Amsterdam, hoping to benefit from their robust extradition laws. He claims that he won’t stand a fair trial due to the press coverage of the case in Scotland. While extradition proceedings take place, Strathclyde Police use the time to build a strong case against Beggs. They return to his flat in the hope of finding additional forensic evidence. At the same time, they uncover more attacks linked to Beggs and make a crucial breakthrough when a new witness comes forward. Back in Amsterdam, Beggs is about to learn his fate – will he be extradited to the UK to stand trial for the murder of Barry Wallace?

programme.title: Limbs in the Loch: Catching a Killer
programme.desc: After 12 months of legal wrangling, William Beggs is finally extradited from the Netherlands to Scotland, where he will be tried for the murder of 18-year-old Barry Wallace at the high court of Edinburgh. Beggs denies the killing, but blood samples belonging to Wallace were found in his flat. The Crown must now prove beyond reasonable doubt that Beggs is the killer and will be relying on a former friend of the accused to give evidence. In accordance with Scots law, the Crown can’t inform the jury of Beggs’s previous convictions. Will William Beggs be found guilty, or will he walk free?

programme.title: Sin City: The Real Las Vegas
programme.desc: Tir Dhondy reveals the realities behind modern Las Vegas. She goes to a high-octane pool party to discover how casinos are cashing in on the party scene.

programme.title: Sin City: The Real Las Vegas
programme.desc: Tir goes even further into the underbelly of Las Vegas to investigate how the reinvention of the city to pull in a new generation of visitors is affecting those who live and work there.

programme.title: Leigh-Anne: Race, Pop and Power
programme.desc: This powerful documentary follows pop star Leigh-Anne Pinnock as she confronts her experience as the only black member of Little Mix, and as a black woman in the music industry. Leigh-Anne talks about the racism she experienced growing up. Both her parents are of Caribbean heritage, and Leigh-Anne identifies as black. She is also aware that having lighter skin and being a celebrity means she is in a more privileged position than others. Leigh-Anne embarks on her own very personal journey to understand how she can use her platform and privilege to combat the profound racism she sees in society around her. After she begins her journey, news of George Floyd’s death and the Black Lives Matter protests start to sweep the world. With the force of a global movement now behind her, Leigh-Anne confronts those closest to her and attempts to bring difficult conversations about black representation right to the top of the music industry.

programme.title: Kingdom
programme.desc: Leopard mother Olimba is bringing up her two cubs in an ideal leopard territory called Nsefu in Zambia. However, her world is soon turned upside down by the arrival of wild dog Storm and her chaotic pack. Storm seems unchallengeable – even dominating hyena Tandala and the rest of her clan. But just when the dogs are beginning to settle into the kingdom and welcome a litter of puppies, an even more powerful force appears on the horizon – lions. These new arrivals are a threat to everyone here – something that is brought into sharp focus when Olimba's young son goes missing...

programme.title: Dynasties
programme.desc: In Senegal, west Africa, live a group of chimpanzees led by an alpha male named David. He has already been alpha for three years - a time when leaders here are usually overthrown. To make matters worse, David has no allies - no-one to help him defend his leadership. As the dry season sets in, the group are forced closer together to survive. But David is now surrounded by rivals who all want his crown and are prepared to kill him for it. David faces brutal battles, has his world engulfed in flames and has to pull off an extraordinary act of deception. In a story of power and politics, can David overcome the threats to his leadership and hold on to the alpha position long enough to sire a possible future heir to his throne?

programme.title: Dynasties

programme.desc: Liv hits the beach for her first ever date, while Charles goes sailing. Dianne meets her first match, and Olivia’s date makes a bold proposition.

programme.title: Better Date Than Never
programme.desc: Olivia invites her date to meet the family, and Liv shares a passionate moment on the harbour. Charles continues his search for love, and Dianne ends her first date on a high.

programme.title: Interior Design Masters with Alan Carr
programme.desc: The eight remaining designers pair up to create uplifting spaces for a homelessness charity in London. They tackle an arts and crafts room, a group workshop room, a wellness area and an employment suite. The charity’s ambassador, Dara Ó Briain, joins Alan to check in on the designers before Michelle and guest judge Sophie Robinson critique the spaces.

programme.title: Kingdom
programme.desc: Leopard mother Olimba is bringing up her two cubs in an ideal leopard territory called Nsefu in Zambia. However, her world is soon turned upside down by the arrival of wild dog Storm and her chaotic pack. Storm seems unchallengeable – even dominating hyena Tandala and the rest of her clan. But just when the dogs are beginning to settle into the kingdom and welcome a litter of puppies, an even more powerful force appears on the horizon – lions. These new arrivals are a threat to everyone here – something that is brought into sharp focus when Olimba's young son goes missing...

programme.title: Dynasties
programme.desc: In Senegal, west Africa, live a group of chimpanzees led by an alpha male named David. He has already been alpha for three years - a time when leaders here are usually overthrown. To make matters worse, David has no allies - no-one to help him defend his leadership. As the dry season sets in, the group are forced closer together to survive. But David is now surrounded by rivals who all want his crown and are prepared to kill him for it. David faces brutal battles, has his world engulfed in flames and has to pull off an extraordinary act of deception. In a story of power and politics, can David overcome the threats to his leadership and hold on to the alpha position long enough to sire a possible future heir to his throne?

programme.title: Dynasties
programme.desc: A mother puma must battle rivals, tackle prey nearly three times her size and endure the wild mountain weather of Patagonia in her bid to raise four cubs – her biggest litter yet.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson and Sammi Kinghorn head to the Vale of Evesham, where fertile soils and a mild microclimate have long made it one of Britain’s most productive growing regions. Early spring brings the so-called hungry gap, but the vale has a long history of producing food, even in these leaner months. From the first spears of its world-famous asparagus to high-tech growers producing food year round, and from historic market gardens to traditional orchards alive with early pollinators, Adam and Sammi explore a landscape shaped by both tradition and innovation. While fresh produce may be scarce elsewhere, the Vale of Evesham is already beginning to flourish. Meanwhile, Charlotte Smith investigates how falling milk prices are leading some dairy farmers to call it a day, despite record exports and booming milk production.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: At the halfway stage of the race, the teams discover their next checkpoint lies within Zaamin National Park, Uzbekistan. To reach it, they must navigate the endless horizons of the vast Kazakh steppe.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: There is lots of planting for the plate at Beechgrove Garden as Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cunningham start growing a wide variety of edible produce. Kirsty is the first of the Beechgrove team to kick off work on her competition plot. Each presenter has been given a sense to appeal to in each of their competition borders, and Kirsty is planting things that will taste fantastic. She is also trying something new to Beechgrove: hops. Meanwhile, Brian provides an update on the veg he sowed at the start of the series and is in his rain garden checking on what survived this year's wet weather. There are all the usual handy hints, and there is a visit to Calum Clunie’s allotment in Leven.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the final leg of his Japanese adventure, Michael explores the history of Hokkaido’s indigenous Ainu people. Travelling east to the Iburi region, an area closely associated with Ainu culture, he visits Lake Shikotsu. Over a traditional meal of salmon soup on the lake shore, he learns about the beliefs and values of the Ainu and how they were forced to assimilate to Japanese society following Hokkaido’s colonisation. After lunch, he is treated to a performance of the ancient Dance of the Cranes. Continuing north to Hokkaido’s capital, Sapporo, Michael enjoys the last evening of his journey in the Susukino district, a Japanese nightlife hotspot. Just along the coast from the port of Otaru on the Sea of Japan, Michael ends his tour with a trip to a famous distillery in the small town of Yoichi.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Warwickshire, farmers take a stand against fly-tippers who have been blighting their land with van-loads of dumped waste. When brothers Tom and Adam Beaty catch two men in the act, tensions rise and police rush to the scene – but will the offenders be held to account? In Northern Ireland’s Mourne mountains, fast-moving wildfires threaten grazing land and livestock, as exhausted firefighters and farmers join forces to bring the flames under control. And in north Wales, reporter Paul Colgan meets Rhianon Bragg, a courageous survivor of domestic abuse whose terrifying ordeal on her rural smallholding exposed the hidden dangers faced by victims living in isolation.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The freedivers take on a search at a castle’s jetty on Windermere, where five years ago a devastated couple lost their treasured wedding ring. Social media detective Mui gets creative in the hope of tracking down the owner of a phone found in the depths, and our crafter Lucy turns a medley of old bottles and jars pulled out of the lake into something quite magical.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: A look at love and relationships in the deaf community, from a couple married for over 50 years to honest conversations about modern dating and finding connection today. Presenter Rolf Choutan is joined by award-winning photographer Becky Bailey, whose work capturing weddings has given her a unique window into the many forms that love can take. Together, they discuss relationships, communication and how connection evolves over time.

programme.title: BBC News
programme.desc: Twenty-four hours a day, the latest national and international stories as they break.

programme.title: Politics Live
programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Impossible
programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive travels 200 miles east of Havana to the historic town of Trinidad – a Unesco world heritage site. Clive meets the octogenarian carpenter whose skills have contributed to keeping this 16th-century city standing, and he learns how to salsa dance with the locals before putting his moves to the test at one of the town’s live music venues. Clive also discovers the dark history of sugar, which was once the main industry here.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The team begins a six-month expedition tracking lions, leopards and cheetahs in the Okavango Delta. Wildlife cinematographer Gordon Buchanan follows one of the largest lion prides in Africa as they hunt to feed 28 hungry mouths, including tiny cubs. Anna Dimitriadis tracks down the Okavango’s most elusive big cat, the cheetah. And local wildlife filmmaker Brad Bestelink reunites with his favourite leopardess, Xudum. A huge wildfire threatens the resident big cats and the team.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and a team of experts invite members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. This programme comes from Mellerstain House in the Scottish Borders, where interesting finds include a valuable majolica dish, a dressing case, and a Lowry doodle.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today Flog It is at the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. There's a photo album of RAF Hendon in the 30s and a rare picture that brings a surprise in the saleroom.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: Paul explores the upper reaches of the River Dee, which rises higher than any river in the UK. In the heart of the Cairngorm Mountains, he learns about writer and mountain lover Nan Shepherd’s passion for the living landscape. He then hears tales about a 100-year-old Jacobite and a Zeppelin airship that attacked a bare mountain. On Royal Deeside, Paul is intrigued by the story of John Brown - Queen Victoria’s very special friend, whose photograph and ring she took to the grave.

programme.title: Planet Earth II
programme.desc: A compilation of the wildlife documentary series presented by David Attenborough. A chance to enjoy the spectacular Planet Earth II, exploring wildlife dramas from across the globe. Ten years on from the groundbreaking original Planet Earth, Planet Earth II shows us life on our planet in entirely new ways. Captured in stunning ultra-high definition detail and using a whole range of new camera technology, this series brings us closer to animals than ever before and reveals new wildlife dramas for the very first time. Planet Earth II is an immersive exploration of the world's jungles, mountains, deserts, islands, grasslands and our newest habitat - cities. As our planet continues to change, never have these wildernesses been as fragile and as a precious as they are today. The series journeys to the four corners of the globe to explore the greatest treasures of our living planet and discover the remarkable ways animals overcome the challenges of surviving in the wildest places on Earth.

programme.title: QI XL
programme.desc: Sandi Toksvig takes a QI look at vices and virtues with Eshaan Akbar, Jo Brand, Rhys James and Alan Davies.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: Unbeknownst to the FBI, a quiet Hungarian immigrant landscaper sits in his home, 250 miles away from Lake Tahoe, Nevada. He has no apparent ties to organised crime and no known record. In 1980, a booby-trapped bomb accompanied by a $3 million ransom note terrorises a casino in Lake Tahoe. Who is the calculating mind behind this sophisticated device and elaborate extortion plan, and what role do his sons play in their father’s dangerous game?

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: Grand Tours of Scotland's Rivers
programme.desc: Paul explores the upper reaches of the River Dee, which rises higher than any river in the UK. In the heart of the Cairngorm Mountains, he learns about writer and mountain lover Nan Shepherd’s passion for the living landscape. He then hears tales about a 100-year-old Jacobite and a Zeppelin airship that attacked a bare mountain. On Royal Deeside, Paul is intrigued by the story of John Brown - Queen Victoria’s very special friend, whose photograph and ring she took to the grave.

programme.title: Planet Earth II
programme.desc: A compilation of the wildlife documentary series presented by David Attenborough. A chance to enjoy the spectacular Planet Earth II, exploring wildlife dramas from across the globe. Ten years on from the groundbreaking original Planet Earth, Planet Earth II shows us life on our planet in entirely new ways. Captured in stunning ultra-high definition detail and using a whole range of new camera technology, this series brings us closer to animals than ever before and reveals new wildlife dramas for the very first time. Planet Earth II is an immersive exploration of the world's jungles, mountains, deserts, islands, grasslands and our newest habitat - cities. As our planet continues to change, never have these wildernesses been as fragile and as a precious as they are today. The series journeys to the four corners of the globe to explore the greatest treasures of our living planet and discover the remarkable ways animals overcome the challenges of surviving in the wildest places on Earth.

programme.title: QI XL

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist
programme.desc: Unbeknownst to the FBI, a quiet Hungarian immigrant landscaper sits in his home, 250 miles away from Lake Tahoe, Nevada. He has no apparent ties to organised crime and no known record. In 1980, a booby-trapped bomb accompanied by a $3 million ransom note terrorises a casino in Lake Tahoe. Who is the calculating mind behind this sophisticated device and elaborate extortion plan, and what role do his sons play in their father’s dangerous game?

programme.title: Newsnight
programme.desc: Insights and global interviews on the crucial news stories of the day.

programme.title: The People’s Piazza: A History of Covent Garden
programme.desc: David Olusoga tells the story of London’s Covent Garden Piazza. Helped by experts and eyewitnesses, he conjures up ghosts of the past - market traders, sex workers and activists.

programme.title: Waves
programme.desc: Tensions beneath the surface cause Florida teen Tyler to sink self-destructively, devastating those closest to him, including his sister Emily.

programme.title: Countryfile
programme.desc: Adam Henson and Sammi Kinghorn head to the Vale of Evesham, where fertile soils and a mild microclimate have long made it one of Britain’s most productive growing regions. Early spring brings the so-called hungry gap, but the vale has a long history of producing food, even in these leaner months. From the first spears of its world-famous asparagus to high-tech growers producing food year round, and from historic market gardens to traditional orchards alive with early pollinators, Adam and Sammi explore a landscape shaped by both tradition and innovation. While fresh produce may be scarce elsewhere, the Vale of Evesham is already beginning to flourish. Meanwhile, Charlotte Smith investigates how falling milk prices are leading some dairy farmers to call it a day, despite record exports and booming milk production.

programme.title: Race Across the World
programme.desc: At the halfway stage of the race, the teams discover their next checkpoint lies within Zaamin National Park, Uzbekistan. To reach it, they must navigate the endless horizons of the vast Kazakh steppe.

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: Long-term addict Bobby heads to rehab, Billy fights for recognition that he has really changed, while Alan is released and heads back to his old ways on Glasgow's streets.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Beechgrove Garden
programme.desc: There is lots of planting for the plate at Beechgrove Garden as Kirsty Wilson and Brian Cunningham start growing a wide variety of edible produce. Kirsty is the first of the Beechgrove team to kick off work on her competition plot. Each presenter has been given a sense to appeal to in each of their competition borders, and Kirsty is planting things that will taste fantastic. She is also trying something new to Beechgrove: hops. Meanwhile, Brian provides an update on the veg he sowed at the start of the series and is in his rain garden checking on what survived this year's wet weather. There are all the usual handy hints, and there is a visit to Calum Clunie’s allotment in Leven.

programme.title: Great Japanese Railway Journeys
programme.desc: On the final leg of his Japanese adventure, Michael explores the history of Hokkaido’s indigenous Ainu people. Travelling east to the Iburi region, an area closely associated with Ainu culture, he visits Lake Shikotsu. Over a traditional meal of salmon soup on the lake shore, he learns about the beliefs and values of the Ainu and how they were forced to assimilate to Japanese society following Hokkaido’s colonisation. After lunch, he is treated to a performance of the ancient Dance of the Cranes. Continuing north to Hokkaido’s capital, Sapporo, Michael enjoys the last evening of his journey in the Susukino district, a Japanese nightlife hotspot. Just along the coast from the port of Otaru on the Sea of Japan, Michael ends his tour with a trip to a famous distillery in the small town of Yoichi.

programme.title: Farm 999
programme.desc: In Warwickshire, farmers take a stand against fly-tippers who have been blighting their land with van-loads of dumped waste. When brothers Tom and Adam Beaty catch two men in the act, tensions rise and police rush to the scene – but will the offenders be held to account? In Northern Ireland’s Mourne mountains, fast-moving wildfires threaten grazing land and livestock, as exhausted firefighters and farmers join forces to bring the flames under control. And in north Wales, reporter Paul Colgan meets Rhianon Bragg, a courageous survivor of domestic abuse whose terrifying ordeal on her rural smallholding exposed the hidden dangers faced by victims living in isolation.

programme.title: Lost and Found in the Lakes
programme.desc: The freedivers take on a search at a castle’s jetty on Windermere, where five years ago a devastated couple lost their treasured wedding ring. Social media detective Mui gets creative in the hope of tracking down the owner of a phone found in the depths, and our crafter Lucy turns a medley of old bottles and jars pulled out of the lake into something quite magical.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: A look at love and relationships in the deaf community, from a couple married for over 50 years to honest conversations about modern dating and finding connection today. Presenter Rolf Choutan is joined by award-winning photographer Becky Bailey, whose work capturing weddings has given her a unique window into the many forms that love can take. Together, they discuss relationships, communication and how connection evolves over time.

programme.desc: The big political issues of the day.

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive travels 200 miles east of Havana to the historic town of Trinidad – a Unesco world heritage site. Clive also discovers the dark history of sugar, which was once the main industry here.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The team begins a six-month expedition tracking lions, leopards and cheetahs in the Okavango Delta. Wildlife cinematographer Gordon Buchanan follows one of the largest lion prides in Africa as they hunt to feed 28 hungry mouths, including tiny cubs. Anna Dimitriadis tracks down the Okavango’s most elusive big cat, the cheetah. And local wildlife filmmaker Brad Bestelink reunites with his favourite leopardess, Xudum. A huge wildfire threatens the resident big cats and the team.

programme.desc: Game show in which 24 players compete across the series, scoring points by answering questions correctly. However, they must avoid the impossible answers, otherwise they will be eliminated from the show until the next day. In each episode there are three rounds, and the three highest scorers from each round play against each other in the final. The winner of this battle faces a £10,000 question.

programme.title: Lightning
programme.desc: Comedian Zoe Lyons presents the electrifyingly fast quiz with a £3,000 jackpot. Six plucky contestants compete across six rounds testing their general knowledge, quick thinking and speedy reactions whilst our ruthless spotlight patrols the studio. The contestants’ motivation in each round is simple: stay out of the light and you’ll be all right!

programme.title: Clive Myrie’s Caribbean Adventure
programme.desc: Clive travels 200 miles east of Havana to the historic town of Trinidad – a Unesco world heritage site. Clive meets the octogenarian carpenter whose skills have contributed to keeping this 16th-century city standing, and he learns how to salsa dance with the locals before putting his moves to the test at one of the town’s live music venues. Clive also discovers the dark history of sugar, which was once the main industry here.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The team begins a six-month expedition tracking lions, leopards and cheetahs in the Okavango Delta. Wildlife cinematographer Gordon Buchanan follows one of the largest lion prides in Africa as they hunt to feed 28 hungry mouths, including tiny cubs. Anna Dimitriadis tracks down the Okavango’s most elusive big cat, the cheetah. And local wildlife filmmaker Brad Bestelink reunites with his favourite leopardess, Xudum. A huge wildfire threatens the resident big cats and the team.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and a team of experts invite members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. This programme comes from Mellerstain House in the Scottish Borders, where interesting finds include a valuable majolica dish, a dressing case, and a Lowry doodle.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: Today Flog It is at the RAF Museum at Hendon in London. There's a photo album of RAF Hendon in the 30s and a rare picture that brings a surprise in the saleroom.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael’s South Korean railway journey continues in Seoul. Travelling across one of the world’s largest metro systems, he heads south to Suwon to visit Samsung’s headquarters, tracing the rise of the family-run company from a small trading business to a global technology giant and symbol of Korea’s postwar economic miracle. Touring a futuristic smart home, Michael explores how innovation now shapes everyday life. Back in central Seoul, he visits the city’s original railway station, built during Japanese rule and now preserved as a cultural space, reflecting the complexities of Korea’s colonial past. In Gangnam, a district propelled to global stardom by a K-pop hit, he explores the international success of Korean popular culture, meeting the boss and dancers at a K-pop academy to understand how Hallyu – the Korean cultural wave – has conquered international audiences. Finally, in Seodaemun, Michael visits a former prison and Independence Park to uncover the story of the March First Movement of 1919, a pivotal moment in Korea’s struggle for independence from Japan, meeting a descendant of a leading resistance figure whose courage helped shape Korea’s struggle for freedom.

programme.title: Flaming Feasts
programme.desc: Chris explores Anglesey with Halen Môn’s smoked water, wild prawns, unique Damara lamb, a kebab-house takeover and the growers shaping the island’s flavours.

programme.title: Planet Earth II
programme.desc: A compilation of the wildlife documentary series presented by David Attenborough. A chance to enjoy the spectacular Planet Earth II, exploring wildlife dramas from across the globe. Ten years on from the groundbreaking original Planet Earth, Planet Earth II shows us life on our planet in entirely new ways. Captured in stunning ultra-high definition detail and using a whole range of new camera technology, this series brings us closer to animals than ever before and reveals new wildlife dramas for the very first time. Planet Earth II is an immersive exploration of the world's jungles, mountains, deserts, islands, grasslands and our newest habitat - cities. As our planet continues to change, never have these wildernesses been as fragile and as a precious as they are today. The series journeys to the four corners of the globe to explore the greatest treasures of our living planet and discover the remarkable ways animals overcome the challenges of surviving in the wildest places on Earth.

programme.desc: Wilf wants a new hobby, so the Piggies suggest golf. But when he and Cornelia compete to see who can hit the ball the farthest, they start breaking things. Cesar and Charlie must find a way to get them to play more gently!

programme.title: Twirlywoos
programme.desc: The Twirlywoos are in a park where they watch a man with a baby in a buggy. The man sits on a bench and entertains the baby with a rattle. When he puts the rattle down, the Twirlywoos take it and pop up behind the man, shaking the rattle. Every time he turns to look, they disappear, much to the baby's amusement! The Twirlywoos return to the boat to find the Drawing Wall. Different hands and feet with different coloured gloves and socks on appear from behind the wall and wave at the Twirlywoos, who wave back. The wall disappears to reveal that the hands and feet all belong to one octopus, who jumps off the wall in surprise and runs out of the door!

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends visit a garden, where they see lots of different vegetables! Meanwhile, Mr Tumble wants to surprise Grandad Tumble by planting some carrot seeds.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: It is sleepybyes time, so the Teletubbies say goodnight to the Tiddlytubbies. But Po isn't tired and goes for a special ride on her scooter.

programme.title: The Baby Club
programme.desc: Giovanna and Baby Bear welcome babies Bella, Olive, Jack, Isobel, Jonas, Leo and their grown-ups to The Baby Club. Inside everyone’s bags in this episode are Soft Toys which are explored through discovery, play, song and story. Grown-ups at home are encouraged to take part by hiding baby appropriate soft toys inside a fabric bag or pillowcase for them to reveal and explore with their baby! The popular song ‘Old McDonald had a farm’ features, as does a story involving Baby Bear. Plus, the Action Song gets everyone moving about, before some calm time with bubbles and the Goodbye Song.

programme.title: Tiny Tunes
programme.desc: In Tall Trees Forest, Lisa and a group of children make pretend cakes, learn British Sign Language signs for pat, cake and baby, and sing and sign the rhyme Pat-a-Cake.

programme.title: I Can Grow It
programme.desc: Novah, Nelly and Aaron are all ears as they discover lots of different sounds in the city centre garden - from tweeting birds and rustling leaves, to cars and a crane!

programme.title: Monster Makes
programme.desc: No, Rebecca isn’t wearing a box on her head - she’s dressed as an astronaut! This gives Murphi an idea. He helps Rebecca discover alien life by creating an alien out of a sock. The Mini Monsters are making skyscapes, Rebecca’s royal relative is looking for something, and the final mega monster make is another space-inspired creation. The Recycling Express and the Tiny Helpers support Rebecca and Murphi as they reach for the stars.

programme.title: Vegesaurs
programme.desc: Ginger joins the baby Pea-Rexes on their expedition to find dinner.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey, Bingo and Mum are enjoying playing Keepy Uppy around the house with their last balloon, when Dad joins in and the game becomes the ultimate test of skill.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are having fun playing games but are surprised to find out that Betty didn’t always enjoy playing. Since her first day at Squirrel Club, she always impressed everyone with her confidence and independence, but at first she didn’t know how to join in with the others. Luckily, Duggee had a great idea to bring all the Squirrels together.

programme.title: Let's Go for a Walk
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers walk along the beach to go paddling in the sea. On the way, they spot some colourful benches, spin like the lights on a lighthouse, make pictures with seashells and even pretend to be crabs!

programme.title: Our Family
programme.desc: It’s Elba’s birthday and sister Iona is planning a very special tea party for her. Iona and Elba decorate the bedroom ready for the big party, and there are lots of balloons and games to enjoy. But Iona and Mum have a secret planned, and Elba is surprised when a robot arrives at the door with her favourite chocolate cake!

programme.title: My World Kitchen
programme.desc: Catfish is a popular fish in Thailand and today Pearlina is serving it with sticky rice. She works hard in the kitchen, combining lots of ingredients to make a special Thai dressing to brush all over the fish. Before they come over, Pearlina's friends taste one of her important ingredients - lemongrass. They're not too keen on it at first, but Pearlina hopes they will like the taste of lemongrass when they taste it in her finished recipe. Pearlina's friends love her beautiful Thai-themed table, and she even finds time to teach them some Thai.

programme.title: Maddie's Do You Know?
programme.desc: In today's episode, Maddie is having a party! She finds out how bubbles work when we blow into bubble mixture. She shows us how the surface tension of water changes when we add soap and how we can stop bubbles from bursting with our hands, and using her slow-motion camera, she shows how bubbles make a sphere shape. Next, Maddie heads to a factory where a party favourite is made - chocolate! We learn how chocolate starts out as a fruit, and we see the chocolates being made for an assortment box. Maddie also uses her special camera to see the superfast robots that put the different chocolates into the right holes in their boxes.

programme.title: Dog Squad
programme.desc: Kika is a golden labrador and a guide dog for her owner Dr Amit, who is blind, which means he cannot see. She is trained to use her super sight to help Dr Amit do as many things as he can by himself. Together, they make the best team! Dr Amit is off to the florist's to buy some flowers for his wife, Seema. To help him get there, Kika enlists the help of top secret 'bumpy bits', the system of clever dots and lines on the pavement that humans call tactile paving. As they navigate their way over a zebra crossing, along a footpath next to a cycle lane, down a stairway near the station and across the road at a pelican crossing, with its top secret spinning cone, Kika explains how the different bumpy bits help her and Dr Amit find their way around town. It’s like reading a secret code. Dr Amit wears shoes that he can feel the different bumps through. And when he finds shoes that are good for the bumps, he buys five pairs! But on their way back from the florist's, Kika finds their path blocked. Can she use her super sight find a new way home in time to give Seema her flowers?

programme.title: Go Wild
programme.desc: Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet one of the world’s smallest bears - Toni, a Malaysian sun bear, or honey bear. They get their name because they love honey! It’s breakfast time for Toni. We see him climbing high in the trees and searching all around his home to find some of the sweet stuff. Next, Aneeshwar and Lizzie meet a flock of colourful rainbow lorikeets. These friendly, brightly coloured and highly chatty birds come to drink nectar from Aneeshwar and Lizzie. Finally, Aneeshwar and Lizzie discover what the wild connection is between these two incredible animals.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Doug's tooth has fallen out, so Jess and Simon tell Waffle about the Tooth Fairy. Waffle longs to meet the Tooth Fairy and his dream comes true.

programme.title: Puffin Rock
programme.desc: Oona practises her digging skills and helps a very impressive dung beetle build his nest.

programme.title: Small Potatoes
programme.desc: Animated series about a group of singing potatoes. The Small Potatoes visit Spain for a flamenco dancing fiesta.

programme.title: Yukee
programme.desc: Stripes and Toad see a beautiful sunrise and decide to write a song about it together. But Stripes wants the song to be rocky, while Toad wants it to be slower. They fall out and go off to write their own songs separately. Can Yukee help them become friends again and create one song together?

programme.title: Maddie + Triggs
programme.desc: Maddie and Triggs are ready for their dinner, but the oven is broken. Luckily, Mum knows how to cook a delicious and balanced meal from fresh ingredients using just the microwave. Before long, the whole family is cooking up a storm with this musical appliance.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Duggee struggles to organise the Squirrels in order of height and keep them focused on the task. Sounds like the Squirrels need some training to improve their concentration.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: The Numberblocks Space Division are on a mission to investigate a signal coming from the depths of space - until a strange planet pulls them off course and splits them into hundreds, tens and ones. How will they escape the planet's rings? One Hundred takes charge and knows just what to do. But can the Numberblocks make the right number to help them teleport away?

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: It’s a snowy day, and Alphablock S is enjoying a ride on a SLED, when she hits a bump and her letter pops out of her dome. Now, S can’t make her ‘s’ sound any more. Her mischievous letter doesn’t want to be caught and enjoys making her friends SLIP and SKID in the snow. Alphablock O has an idea. T challenges the letter S to a race up the hill. The other letters arrive at the TOP first, and then jump out to grab the ‘s’ to make STOP. Now, they can put it back in the right SPOT in S’s dome.

programme.title: Something Special
programme.desc: Justin and his friends visit a cafe and find George from the CBeebies House there! Meanwhile, Baker Tumble plans a surprise tea party for Mr Tumble.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: The Teletubbies enjoy a game of What's Your Name? Later, there's a surprise when a bowl of Tubby Custard joins in with the game!

programme.title: Ranger Hamza's Eco Quest
programme.desc: Ranger Hamza and the Ramblers discover how stinging nettles play an important role in the environment. They find out that a nettle’s sting can help protect it as well as some insects that shelter on them. They learn that nettles can also be food for some animals too. On the way, they try some nettle tea and pretend to be stinging nettles, trying to keep Ranger Hamza’s Mr Fox away!

programme.title: Football Fantastics
programme.desc: Elvis refuses to play football after his lucky, stinky socks are washed. Evie B leads the hunt for the smelliest smell in the Den so they can make the socks stinky again.

programme.title: Grace's Amazing Machines
programme.desc: In this superfast episode, CBeebies’ very own motorbike rider Grace shows off three amazing machines that are powered by electricity! Grace rides a very unusual electric motorbike, checks out a solar plane and then drives an eco racer!

programme.title: Dodge's Pup School
programme.desc: It's been a busy morning at Pup School, so Miss Collie decides it is best for the class to spend some quiet time doing calm activities. The problem is that all the activities sound very exciting to Dodge. He wants to do them all, and at the same time too!

programme.title: Love Monster
programme.desc: Love Monster and Tiniest Fluffiest Bunny enter an inventing contest, but they cannot agree on whose idea to make, so they decide to go it alone.

programme.title: Octonauts: Above & Beyond
programme.desc: Peso and Dashi help a flying fox mother and pup survive the heat in an Australian swamp.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: When a very sleepy Tommy Brock is hoisted up into the Squirrel Camp, Peter and friends must work out how to get the snoozing brute back down to earth before he wakes up!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: It is a rainy day in the clubhouse, which means it’s a perfect day for a board game. Duggee introduces the Squirrels to one of his favourite games, but it might be just a little bit too complex for them.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: When Sunny doesn’t want to see the Sweetwood Band, even though he loves music, Vida helps him out with earmuffs and he gets to enjoy the show!

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea has made fake fortune cookies for Supertato, Broccoli and Carrot to trick them into leaving the supermarket so she can lock them out! Luckily, Carrot has a plan to make some fortune cookies of her own that will get Evil Pea to reopen the doors.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings want to take a beautiful family portrait with their pop, but Weasy can’t help making faces and monkeying around. The ducklings decide to take a surprise photo of him so that he’ll look natural.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Preston needs to knock down his shed, and Mojo has the wrecking ball to do it. But first, Mojo and Bo have to get it all the way across town, which is harder than it sounds!

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey’s Father’s Day card has to be perfect, but she can’t decide what to draw.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: Nervous about public speaking, Looph builds a robot to deliver a science talk in her place, but her friends are determined to help her do it herself.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey and Bingo try to taste each other's each ice creams, but they're starting to melt.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: When Dr Ollie discovers the Story Bus is delayed, he vows to save the day by inventing a new story to tell Miss Hoolie and the children.

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: It's the hottest day of the year and Waffle is eating ice cream to cool down. Outside in the sweltering heat, Simon turns on the sprinkler to help everyone cool down, but poor Waffle doesn't like the sprinkler and darts through the hole in the fence to Mrs Hobbs's garden, looking for shade. The Brooklyn-Bells try to coax him back, but he refuses to return.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi wants her dads to stop doing chores and to dance with her. She wishes to be the oldest so that she can set the rules. Suddenly, Jake and Dash turn into babies, leaving Rafi in charge! It’s funny at first, but soon the mess grows. Rafi realises being a grown-up means taking responsibility. She cleverly mixes tidying with dancing, showing them chores can be fun too. When the wish ends, her dads return to normal and are proud of Rafi’s maturity and teamwork.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo has drawn a picture to show Great Gran Gran over a video call, but just as she’s about to show it, the internet goes down! Gran Gran suggests they post JoJo’s picture to Great Gran Gran in Saint Lucia. JoJo learns why a letter takes such a long time to travel halfway across the world.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Duck isn't careful enough with his favourite toy robot.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: Tiny, Small and Baby Soup Dragon are outside playing when they hear the sound of something approaching from space. They look up and gaze in awe as they see a large space module hurtling towards the planet. It gets slower and slower as it nears them until eventually it lands a little way away, a door opens and from out of it steps a strange creature in a space suit – they don’t know what it is but we can see it’s a human astronaut! They rush back underground to tell the others.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa hear a beautiful sound and wonder where it’s coming from. They head to the Play Tree, where they choose some pan pipes to play with. One of the pipes sounds like the beautiful sound, and when they play that note, the sound replies. They don’t find the source at Yummy Time, although they hear the sound again. On the Lullaby Lake, they discover that Elewhale is making the lovely noise.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: The Tombliboos are indoors playing with their bricks. They decide to make three towers. Makka Pakka is making piles of stones, but he needs another one to make three piles of three stones. Upsy Daisy arrives with a present for Makka Pakka, a stone which she found in her bed. Now Makka Pakka can complete his piles of three stones.

programme.title: CBeebies Bedtime Stories
programme.desc: Guz Khan reads a story about a little boy's admiration for his dad's beard.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: This Is CBeebies
programme.desc: Programmes start at 6.00am.

programme.title: Roots and Fruits
programme.desc: Live from the Roots and Fruits theatre, it’s the rock 'n' roll star Parsley performing Rise Up with Me about all things rock.

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Bing finds a frog in the garden and wants to keep it, so he and Sula make the frog a 'house' in a bucket. But Froggy doesn't like her new home and hops out. Maybe they've not thought enough about what Froggy really needs in her home.

programme.title: Teletubbies
programme.desc: It's Teletubby Circus time! Tinky Winky balances on the tight rope, Dipsy juggles, Laa-Laa flies on the trapeze and Po is a funny clown.

programme.title: Tee and Mo
programme.desc: Tee races to complete his Action Ape jigsaw puzzle, only to discover that there's one piece missing. It's now up to Tee and Mo to find a creative way of completing the jigsaw picture.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea lures Supertato and Tomato into her cave of frosted doom. Can they find the courage to avoid her traps and retrieve The Lost Candle of Birthdays for Tomato’s Museum?

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: Sula and Amma surprise Bing to show him Sula's sparkly painted butterfly face. Bing also wants a painted face, one that looks like Biteysaurus, and Sula says she can do it for him. Sula begins smothering his face in Bitey's signature green, but when she accidentally adds purple spots, Bing is horrified! He wants Sula to go home. But then Flop adds some teeth to Bing's Biteysaurus, so he can really be Bitey.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: Ted the bus wants to be faster, and Mojo swops every top to try to make it happen. But it’s Bo’s homemade rocket that gives Ted the boost he needs... all the way into space!

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: Follow the twists and turns of a brightly coloured straw as it meanders past the wall frames and around the Clubhouse. Next, the Squirrels have prepared a fascinating guessing game, and there's another episode of Agony and Eggstacy. Finally, it is Hedgeley’s birthday, and Duggee wants to prepare something special for him to eat on this important day. After that, King Tiger invites everyone to play copy the king.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels are crafting in the Clubhouse when Betty saves Tag from throwing water across the table instead of glitter. We learn quickly that Tag, although full of enthusiasm and energy, has not always been the best listener. He was great at discovering new things, and everyone wanted to join in with him - but getting easily distracted would land him in an array of trouble.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Bluey’s Father’s Day card has to be perfect, but she can’t decide what to draw.

programme.title: Go Jetters
programme.desc: Glitch creates big trouble with a little pyramid when he and the Go Jetters visit Egypt.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit
programme.desc: Peter and his friends try to find the perfect place to eat the radishes they took from Mr McGregor's garden, but there is a radish robber on their tails!

programme.title: Octonauts
programme.desc: Animated deep sea adventure series. Captain Barnacles and his intrepid band of explorers roam the oceans in search of adventure and fun. When Captain Barnacles and most of the crew are unable to return to base, it's up to Peso and Tweak to remove a stuck hermit crab from its shell.

programme.title: Numberblocks
programme.desc: Are you sitting comfortably? Then we'll begin a bedtime story all about the first five Numberblocks. Learn all about the numbers one, two, three, four and five with Numberblocks One to Five.

programme.title: Alphablocks
programme.desc: T has such a tip-top time making words with his friends that he invites S to join him - and soon wishes he hadn't. If only he could start the whole day over again! This episode has fun with the 'st' blend and the words top, tub, tag, stop, stub, stag, lost and best.

programme.title: Nick Cope's Popcast
programme.desc: Nick and Norman are going for a neighbourhood stroll when Nick discovers a stone in his shoe. How did it get there? The stone makes Nick do a funny dance, and the Popcasters help to write a song to go with his shaky leg.

programme.title: Playtime Towers
programme.desc: Lift is in a cheeky mood and makes Bella a snack of one little pea! In the Fortress of Fun, Kingsley and Queenie have fun looking for peas with the Playtimers in their Pea Party game, whilst in the Cloud Kitchen, a pea pod from Foggy reminds Patch of the time he spent at the Veggieville Music Festival. In Boxtropolis, Sketch and the Playtimers make Wiggle Wiggle Caterpillars using bouncy balls!

programme.title: Bing
programme.desc: As Bing gets ready to go to Sula's house, he feels sneezy and hot, so Flop decides that Bing needs to stay at home and keep his germs to himself. Even though Bing is soon tucked up on the sofa with a hot honey and lemon drink, he's very disappointed that he can't play with Sula. But Sula and Amma bring him a carroty bagel to wish him a speedy recovery.

programme.title: Yakka Dee!
programme.desc: Dee encourages a friend to say ‘castle’, and we go on a whirlwind word adventure. We visit lots of castles. A tall and small castle, a sandcastle and a spooky castle - boo! We see Dee in a castle in the clouds and bouncing on a bouncy castle! And have you ever seen a banana castle before? The journey is repeated with some special surprises along the way, and everyone has a boogie when Dee’s friend finally succeeds in saying today’s word.
